Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:11:1.hebrew: וחללו על אחר - אמר זה תחת זה, ובעל מום יוצא לחולין:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:11:1.english: And he desacralized it onto another - He said, "This in place of this," and a blemished animal goes out to unconsecrated status.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:11:2.hebrew: סלקא דעתך כו' - והכי קאמר קרא: אם על האחד עבר זמן איחור, חייב, ולא שיצטרפו הוא וחילופיו לג' רגלים:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:11:2.english: It might enter your mind, etc. - And this is what the verse is saying: if the time of delay has passed for the one [offering] alone, he is liable; but [the verse does] not [mean] that it and its substitute combine to make up three festivals.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:13:1.hebrew: שעברה שנתו - מצותו בתוך שנתו, שנאמר (דברים ט״ו:כ׳) לפני ה' אלהיך תאכלנו שנה בשנה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:13:1.english: Whose year has passed - Its mitzvah [of being eaten] is within its [first] year, as it is stated (Deuteronomy 15:20): "Before the Lord your God you shall eat it, year by year."

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:13:2.english: Like disqualified consecrated animals - Like [an animal] with a blemish.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:13:3.hebrew: ויפסל - הואיל ועבר עליו ואיחרו, שהרי אין שנה בלא שלשה רגלים ברוב שנים:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:13:3.english: And let it be disqualified - Since [a festival] passed over it and he delayed it, for there is no year without three festivals in most years.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:14:1.hebrew: מקיש בכור למעשר - במעשר דגן קא משתעי קרא:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:14:1.english: It compares the firstborn to the tithe - The verse is speaking of the tithe of grain.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:14:2.hebrew: מה מעשר אינו נפסל כו' - דכתיב (שם יד) מקצה שלש שנים וגו', אם שהה מעשרותיו שנה ראשונה ושניה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:14:2.english: Just as maaser is not disqualified, etc. - For it is written (ibid. 14): "At the end of three years, etc." This applies even if he kept his tithes [without bringing them] through the first year and the second.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:15:1.english: Acceptance - Whether for atonement or as a gift.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:15:2.english: Say that they should not be accepted favorably - Since he brought them in transgression.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:1:1.hebrew: כפסח דמו - וברגל ראשון יעבור עליהן:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:1:1.english: They are like the Paschal offering - And [the law of "you shall not delay" applies to them] when the first festival passes over them.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:2:1.hebrew: מנא הני מילי - דאכל הנך דתניא במתניתא לעיל איכא בל תאחר:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:2:1.english: From where are these matters [derived]? - That for all of these that were taught in the baraita above, there is [the prohibition of] "do not delay."

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:2:2.english: A vow - "It is incumbent upon me."

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:2:3.english: A gift-offering - [where one says:] "This [animal is an offering]."

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:3:1.hebrew: נאמר להלן נדר - "ואם נדר או נדבה" וגו':
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:3:1.english: It is stated below "neder" (vow) - "And if a vow or a voluntary offering," etc.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:4:1.english: These are the values and the valuations, etc. - For they are consecrated property for the Temple maintenance, and all of them belong to the Lord, and the priests have no share in them.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:4:2.hebrew: הוא ולא חילופיו - עליו אתה עובר ולא על חילופיו, ולקמיה מפרש לה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:4:2.english: He, but not his substitutes - You transgress [the prohibition of delay] with regard to it, but not with regard to its substitutes. And later [the Gemara] explains this.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:4:3.english: These are sin-offerings and guilt-offerings - For they are demanded of you, since they are an obligation incumbent upon you.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:4:4.hebrew: ועולות ושלמים - כגון עולת ראיה ושלמי חגיגה שהן חובה, דאלו דנדר ונדבה ברישא דקרא כתיבי, וה"ה נמי לבכור ולמעשר ופסח שהן חובה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:4:4.english: And burnt offerings and peace offerings - For example, the burnt offering of appearance and the peace offerings of the festival, which are obligatory, for those [offerings] of a vow and a freewill offering are written in the beginning of the verse. And the same applies as well to the firstborn, the tithe, and the Paschal offering, which are obligatory.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:5:1.hebrew: ה' אלהיך אלו צדקות ומעשרות - דהא קרא יתירא הוא, דהוה ליה למכתב "כי דרוש ידרשנו", וכבר ה' כתוב למעלה במקרא, נדרוש ביה לאתויי צדקות ומעשרות שכתוב בהן שם זה: "ולך תהיה צדקה לפני ה' אלהיך" (דברים כ״ד:י״ג), "ואכלת לפני ה' אלהיך מעשר דגנך" (שם יד):
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:5:1.english: "The Lord your God" – these are charity and tithes - For this phrase is superfluous in the verse, since it should have written only "for He will surely seek it," and the Name "the Lord" was already written earlier in the verse. Therefore we expound it to include charity and tithes, in which this Name is written: "And it shall be righteousness for you before the Lord your God" (Deuteronomy 24:13), and "And you shall eat before the Lord your God the tithe of your grain" (ibid. 14).

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:5:2.hebrew: מעמך זה לקט שכחה ופאה - שהן חלקו של עני, דכתיב ביה (שמות כ״ב:כ״ד) את העני עמך:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:5:2.english: "From you" – this refers to leket, shikhchah, and pe'ah - For these are the portion of the poor person, about whom it is written (Exodus 22:24): "the poor person with you."

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:5:3.hebrew: ולא בקרבנך חטא - אין הקרבן נפסל בכך:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:5:3.english: But not a sin in your offering - The offering is not disqualified by this.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:6:1.english: Substitutes of a burnt offering - For example, it was lost and he set aside another in its place; the first was found, and atonement was effected through it.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:6:2.hebrew: מקרב קרבי - וכיון דקרבה, הרי היא קרבן לעצמה, ו"לשלמו" קרינא ביה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:6:2.english: It is sacrificed - And since it is sacrificed, it is an offering in its own right, and we apply to it [the verse's expression] "to pay it."

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:7:1.hebrew: חילופי חטאת - שכיפרו בעליה, מחמש חטאות המתות היא, ופשיטא דלא עבר עליה בבל תאחר:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:7:1.english: The exchanges of a sin offering - [This means a sin offering] whose owners have already been atoned for [by another offering]. It is one of the five sin offerings that are left to die. And it is obvious that one does not transgress "do not delay" with regard to it.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:7:2.hebrew: חילופי תודה - וכגון שנתערבה בראשונה, וקי"ל על זבח התודה, חלות התודה טעונה לחם, ולא חליפתה ולא תמורתה טעונין לחם:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:7:2.english: The substitutes of a thanksgiving offering - For example, where [the substitute] became mixed up with the first [offering]. And we hold regarding the thanksgiving sacrifice that the loaves of the thanksgiving offering require bread, but neither its substitute nor its exchange requires bread.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:8:1.hebrew: ומתה אחת מהן - שאם היו שתיהן קיימות, מביאן ומביא ארבעים חלות כמשפט התודה, ואומר הרי הלחם הזה לשם אותה שהיא תודה, ושחיטת התודה תקדש ארבעים כמשפטה. אבל מתה, אין לחברתה תקנה (והיכי) ממעט קרא מבל תאחר:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 5b:8:1.english: And one of them died - For if both were alive, he would bring both of them and bring forty loaves according to the law of the thanksgiving offering, and say, "This bread is for whichever of them is the thanksgiving offering," and the slaughter of the thanksgiving offering would sanctify the forty loaves according to their law. But if one died, its fellow has no remedy. (And how) the verse excludes it from [the prohibition of] "do not delay."

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 5b:12:1.hebrew: שהומם בתוך הרגל - ואין בל תאחר אלא בכל הרגל:
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 5b:12:1.english: That became blemished during the festival - And [the prohibition of] "do not delay" applies only after the entire festival [has passed].

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 5b:14:1.hebrew: מה מעשר אינו נפסל משנה לחברתה - פירש בקונטרס דכתיב "מקצה שלש שנים תוציא את כל מעשר תבואתך", אם שהה מעשרות שנה ראשונה ושניה. ואפילו למאי דפרישית לעיל דאיכא בבל תאחר במעשר שהופרש ולא נתנו, וקרא דשנת הביעור אצטריך לאותו שלא הופרש, מ"מ בכולהו משתעי קרא דמתבער. וקצת תימה בכולה שמעתין: מהיכא תיתי לן דנפסל, דאיצטריך קרא דאינו נפסל? וכן אותו בלא ירצה, ואין מאחר נדרו בלא ירצה, למה לי:
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 5b:14:1.english: Just as maaser is not disqualified from one year to the next - Rashi explained in the Kuntres that it is written (Deuteronomy 14:28): "At the end of three years you shall bring out all the tithe of your produce" — [this applies] if he kept the tithes [without giving them] in the first and second year. And even according to what I explained above, that there is [a violation of] "you shall not delay" for maaser that was separated and not given, and that the verse of the year of removal is needed for [maaser] that was not separated, nevertheless the verse speaks of removal with regard to all of them. It is somewhat astonishing, throughout this entire passage: from where would we have thought that it becomes disqualified, such that a verse was needed to teach that it is not disqualified? And likewise, regarding that [teaching derived from] "it shall not be accepted" — and [the teaching that] one who delays his vow [is derived from] "it shall not be accepted" — why do I need it?

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 5b:15:1.hebrew: קדשים דבני הרצאה נינהו - דעולה מכפרת על חייבי עשה, כדאמרינן בפרק קמא דזבחים (דף ז: ושם):
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 5b:15:1.english: Sacrificial offerings are of the kind that bring acceptance [before God] - For an olah atones for those who are liable for [violating] a positive commandment, as we say in the first chapter of Zevachim (7b, and there).

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 5b:3:1.hebrew: ונאמר להלן אם נדר או נדבה - הוה מצי לאתויי מהאי עניינא גופיה, דכתיב ביה (דברים כג) "כאשר נדרת נדבה":
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 5b:3:1.english: And it is stated below, "If a vow or a freewill offering" - [The Gemara] could have derived it from this very passage, in which it is written (Deuteronomy 23): "Just as you vowed, a freewill offering."

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 5b:4:1.hebrew: ערכין וחרמין והקדשות - בכולהו כתיב לה': גבי ערכין כתיב בערכך נפשות לה' (ויקרא כ״ז:כ״ח-כ״ט), ובחרמין כתיב (שם) קדש קדשים הוא לה'. וגבי חרמי כהן נמי דריש ליה בבכורות בר"פ כל פסולי המוקדשים (בכורות ד' לב.). ובהקדשות כתיב (שם) איש כי יקדיש את ביתו קדש לה'. וא"ת, מהאי טעמא נמי תיפוק ליה חטאת ואשם ועולה ושלמים, כדדרשינן נמי לקמן בשמעתין מדכתיב לה' אלהיך בקרא דמוצא שפתיך תשמור? וי"ל [דלקמן, דאית ליה קרא אחרינא לקדשי בדק הבית מאשר דברת, מוקי ליה קרא דלה' אלהיך לחטאות ואשמות, דמסתבר; אבל הכא] אי לאו דכתיב דרוש ידרשנו בחטאת ואשם, הוה מוקמינן בהו האי קרא, ולא הוה שמעינן ערכין חרמין והקדשות [וליכא למלפינהו נמי מדרוש ידרשנו, דלא משמע אלא שבא על חטא]:
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 5b:4:1.english: Valuations, devoted items, and consecrated items - In all of them "to the Lord" is written. Regarding valuations, it is written: "According to your valuation of persons, to the Lord" (Leviticus 27:28-29). And regarding devoted items, it is written (ibid.): "It is most holy to the Lord." And regarding the devoted items of a priest, [the Gemara] also derives this in Bekhorot, in the beginning of the chapter "Kol Pesulei HaMukdashin" (Bekhorot 32a). And regarding consecrated items, it is written (ibid.): "If a man consecrates his house, holy to the Lord." But if you say: For this reason, let [the Gemara] also derive from it [the cases of] a sin offering, a guilt offering, a burnt offering, and a peace offering, just as we also derive later in our passage from the fact that "the Lord your God" is written in the verse "That which has gone out of your lips you shall keep"? And one can answer [that later, where [the Gemara] has another verse for consecrations for the Temple's maintenance, "from that which you have vowed," it establishes the verse "the Lord your God" as referring to sin offerings and guilt offerings, since that is the reasonable reading; but here,] had it not been written "you shall surely seek it" regarding a sin offering and a guilt offering, we would have established this verse as referring to them, and we would not have learned [the cases of] valuations, devoted items, and consecrated items. [And one cannot derive them from "you shall surely seek it" either, since it implies only [an offering] that comes on account of a sin.]

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 5b:4:2.hebrew: אלו חטאות ואשמות - שהן נדרשין ממך, שהרי הם מוטלין חובה עליך; ועולות ושלמים, כגון עולת ראיה ושלמי חגיגה, שהם חובה, דאלו נדרים ונדבות מ״כי תדור נדר״ נפקי. ותימה: שלמי חגיגה וראיה זמנא קביעא להו, דעבר הרגל ולא חג אינו חייב באחריותו, וא"כ אם אקרביה אקרביה וכו', כדאקשינן לעיל גבי פסח. וי"ל דמ"מ היכא דהופרשו ולא הקריבם, קאי עלייהו בבל תאחר, כיון שלא נפסלו בכך. וי"מ דנפקא להו חטאת מדכתיב לשון דרישה גבי חטאת, דכתיב (ויקרא י׳:ט״ז) "דרש דרש משה"; ואשם, עולה ושלמים, דאיתקוש בהיקישא דזאת התורה בסוף התודה (מנחות דף פב: ושם). ולא יתכן, דא"כ נדרים ונדבות נמי, ובכור ומעשר ופסח נמי, תיפוק מהתם, דכולהו איתקוש:
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 5b:4:2.english: These are sin-offerings and guilt-offerings - For they are "demanded of you," since they are imposed upon you as an obligation; and burnt-offerings and peace-offerings, such as the burnt-offering of appearance and the peace-offering of the festival, which are obligatory, as opposed to vows and free-will offerings, which derive from "when you vow a vow." But this is astonishing: the peace-offerings of the festival and of appearance have a fixed time, for one who let the festival pass without celebrating it is not liable for [replacing] it, and if so, if he offered it, he offered it, etc., as we asked above regarding the Pesach offering. And one can answer that, in any case, where they were set aside and he did not offer them, he transgresses "you shall not delay" with respect to them, since they were not disqualified by this. Some say that the sin-offering derives from the fact that the language of seeking (derishah) is written regarding the sin-offering, as it is written (Leviticus 10:16): "Moses diligently inquired (darosh darash)"; and the guilt-offering, burnt-offering, and peace-offering [derive] from the fact that they are linked by the analogy of "This is the law" at the end of the [passage on the] thanksgiving-offering (Menachot 82b, there). But this is not plausible, for if so, vows and free-will offerings too, and the firstborn, tithe, and Pesach offering too, should be derived from there, since all of them are linked by analogy.

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 5b:5:1.hebrew: ומעשרות ובכור - מעשר ובכור מכי דרוש ידרשנו לא נפקא, דלא דמי חיובא דידהו לחיובא דחטאת ואשם, דאי לית ליה בכור ומעשר לא מיחייב בהו. ופסח לא גרסינן הכא, דאי בשלמי פסח כרב ששת, מהיכא דנפקא שלמים נפקא להו; ומיהו יש לחלק:
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 5b:5:1.english: And tithes and the firstborn - [The obligation of] tithes and the firstborn is not derived from "you shall surely seek [it]" (Deuteronomy 23:22), because their obligation is not similar to the obligation of a sin-offering and a guilt-offering; for if one has no firstborn animal or tithe, he is not obligated in them. And we do not have the reading "Pesach" here, for if it refers to the peace-offerings of Pesach, in accordance with Rav Sheshet, they are derived from the same source from which peace-offerings are derived. However, one can distinguish [between them].

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 5b:7:1.hebrew: אי חליפי חטאת למיתה אזלא - ואי חליפי אשם, לרעייה אזלא, דקי"ל (נזיר כה:) כל שבחטאת מתה, באשם רועה. ולר"ת דמפרש דמן הדין באשם קרב עולה, א"כ מקרב קרבי:
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 5b:7:1.english: If [it is] the substitutes of a sin offering, it goes to die - And if [it were] the substitutes of a guilt offering, it would go to graze, for we hold (Nazir 25b) that whatever [animal] in the case of a sin offering dies, in the case of a guilt offering grazes. But according to Rabbeinu Tam, who explains that by law a guilt offering is offered as a burnt offering, then it would indeed be offered.
